narrative: During the 2020s, Black and African women's hairstyles and hair culture continue to thrive, reflecting a deep connection to their heritage and identity. The natural hair movement remains strong, with many embracing their textured locks in all its forms - waves, curls, coils, and kinks. Hairstyles like afros, cornrows, and box braids are staples of African braiding practice, not only for their aesthetic appeal but also as a means to protect and preserve the health of Afro-textured hair. Dreadlocks and locs have also gained popularity, with many women embracing this style as a way to celebrate their natural texture. The Jheri curl, once a popular chemical treatment in the 1980s and early 1990s, has largely been replaced by more natural hairstyles that prioritize health and self-expression. As African-American culture continues to evolve, hairstyles have become an integral part of identity, community, and resistance - a testament to the power of hair as a symbol of pride, resilience, and cultural heritage.
